runtime_status_notes: V4 closes the provider-local D3D9Ex question: DXVK 3.1.1 Create9Ex promotion works, but legacy D3D9 shared-handle DirectGPU interop does not become usable on this native Windows run.
DirectGPU failure is now transport-specific, not an Ex-promotion failure.
Vehicle selector color remains correct on DXVK with D3D9Ex=1, weakening the hypothesis that the common Ex promotion/state layer alone causes the DX9Ex color bug.
The HMD pacing failure persists because V4 remains on SBS/Desktop Duplication; sampled gameplay XR cadence is frequently around one frame per ~34-36 ms.

rationale: The branch IAT hook resolves Direct3DCreate9Ex from the same d3d9 provider that supplied Direct3DCreate9 and explicitly allows third-party provider-local Ex.
The pinned stock DXVK 3.1.1 x86 d3d9.dll exports Direct3DCreate9Ex.
A successful promotion can reuse the existing four-slot D3D9Ex-to-D3D11 zero-copy transport and is a smaller, better-isolated test than designing a new transport immediately.
The test also discriminates the DX9Ex vehicle-color issue: if color regresses only after provider-local Ex promotion, the Ex compatibility/state layer becomes the primary suspect.

collector_fix.root_cause: PowerShell variable names are case-insensitive. The portable collector assigned to $host, which collides with the built-in read-only $Host variable.

v6_fix: Rename collector process variable from $host to $vrHostProcess; static check rejects any remaining assignment to $host.
Retain named cross-process mutex so crashed collectors do not leave a stale file lock.
Stage the completed session outside the source tree before Compress-Archive.
Run both detached watcher and synchronous post-game collection; mutex de-duplicates them.
Keep COLLECT_DXVK_EX_LOGS_NOW.cmd as a safe retry path for the same session.
Write COLLECTOR_SELFTEST.txt plus explicit GAME_EXIT_CODE and LOG_COLLECTION status.
